reason: Verified end to end; every load-bearing claim holds. (1) CSS: b.css:633-642 sets .b-switch{font-weight:600} for the project name; b.css:643-650 (.b-switch span) overrides font-family, font-size, line-height, letter-spacing, text-transform and color and NOT weight. (2) Faces: fonts.css declares exactly three @font-face rules - Geist 400, Geist 600, Geist Mono 400 - and fonts/ holds exactly three woff2 files. No Geist Mono 600 exists. document.fonts confirms [Geist 400 loaded, Geist 600 loaded, Geist Mono 400 loaded]. (3) Sweep: I walked every element in all fourteen states at 1440 and computed family+weight. Exactly ONE element in the whole document computes a mono family above 400: the leaf SPAN 'one of three', font-weight 600, 11px, family "Geist Mono". It is present and visible at 390, 768, 1152, 1280 and 1440, on owner-flight, owner-empty, owner-editing, owner-undone, owner-draft and publish. (4) The synthesis is real, not theoretical: element screenshots at deviceScaleFactor 4 of the live string at 600 and at 400 differ sharply - glyph pixel area rises from 2791 to 4158 px (+49%) with the advance unchanged (100.328125px at both, canvas measureText 79.1999 at both), which is the exact signature of Chromium emboldening the 400 outlines rather than selecting a real face. At 3x in situ 'ONE OF THREE' plainly out-weighs its neighbours. (5) The register clash is measured, not asserted: on owner-empty the bar carries 'one of three' at x=437,y=112 and 'Nothing to preview yet' at x=1070,y=111 - same line, same 11px, same 1.76px tracking, same rgba(255,255,255,0.62), same uppercase - one at a synthesised 600 and one at a real 400. Same story on owner-flight against 'Today is 16 July' and 'Behind you'. (6) The lock is breached verbatim: lock.md:90-91 reads 'Geist 400 and 600, Geist Mono 400. Three faces, no others, no third weight.' (7) Both gates are genuinely blind, so this is not a restatement. audit.mjs:249 tests `weight` against [400,600] and families separately at line 468 - it never tests the PAIR against what @font-face actually loads, so mono-600 passes as two individually-legal values; and the advance is unchanged so no ramp/tracking check moves. interaction-check.mjs:2038 keys the uppercase register on fontFamily|fontSize|letterSpacing|color and omits fontWeight, so it counts this string as the same object as the real 400 labels and 'the heads are one object' still passes. Not out of scope: the fix REMOVES a weight rather than adding one. Not taste: a browser-synthesised face is a mechanical defect. Not made worse by the fix: the advance is identical at both weights, so nothing reflows, and the interaction-check key never read weight.
sharpenedFix: One line: add `font-weight: 400;` to the `.b-switch span` rule in b.css (currently lines 643-650), directly under `font-family: var(--mono);`, then regenerate master.html with build.mjs - never hand-edit master. Measured consequence: zero. The advance is byte-identical at 400 and 600 (100.328125px), so nothing reflows; the string keeps 11px, --lead-label, 0.16em, uppercase and --fore-62, and becomes property-for-property identical to .b-where and .b-inert. Two optional hardenings, both cheap: (a) .b-where, .b-inert and .b-switch span now declare the same six properties three times - fold them into one shared selector so the label register cannot drift again; (b) close the gate hole that let this through, by having audit.mjs assert the family+weight PAIR against the set of loaded @font-face descriptors (build it from document.fonts) rather than checking families and weights on separate lists - that turns 'no synthesised face' into something mechanical rather than something a seat has to catch by eye.
